questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your traineeship destination (city/region)? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available at your traineeship destination (organization/city/region)? *
questions.answer: I joined a yoga class outside my work, but was also active in the thins my work organised. I even helped making the office greener with another colleague.

questions.question: Which non-academic activities would you recommend to future trainees visiting the same destination (organization/city/region)? Why? *
questions.answer: The office organised a lot of social meeting opportunities. Join the sports and social events. They are really nice to get to know your colleagues.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting trainees see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Visit many terraces and nice restaurants in Maastricht. Take lot of walks in the city. In the weekend go biking outside the city or go for a walk in the Ardennen.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your trainee host? *
questions.answer: Easy, there were a lot of sport acitivities organised. I also joined this committee and gave some yoga classes and participated in a table tennis tournament. I also joined some differs, after work drinks and sat together during lunch. Every day there was lunch at 12:00 and colleagues get u from your office if you forget.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of the destination (city/country)? *
questions.answer: Good, everybody is really friendly and helpful.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with locals? *
questions.answer: Join a committee at the office or join a sports association. There is also a European student association with many international students called ESN. IFMSA is also interesting for medical related students, but it is unsure if they accept someone for only a year.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: none.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The helpfulness of people.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going on a traineeship to the same city/region? *
questions.answer:
- Get a (rental) bike
- Enjoy the city center as much as u can
- join social acitivities as the office.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future traineeship students? *
questions.answer: Be very proactive in your own learning as dutch supervisors might expect a lot of independence.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your traineeship experience? *
questions.answer: Being very free and independent in my research. Not only did I figure out most of the analysis myself, but I was also able to pick the techniques and research points myself.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the traineeship? *
questions.answer: Learning MRI analysis and coding with no background.

questions.question: Is there anything UCPH could have done different (before/during/after) in regard to the traineeship experience? *
questions.answer: Not specifically.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
